intent.raw_query: Morocco Marrakech and Sahara, $1000 solo, 7 days, March 2026

selected_hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)

experiences.name: Djemaa el-Fna Square & Medina Exploration
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in the sensory chaos of Marrakech's UNESCO-listed main square. Watch snake charmers, storytellers, and musicians by day, then witness the square transform into a massive open-air food market at sunset. Wander the labyrinthine souks of the ancient medina, haggling for spices, leather goods, and handwoven textiles.

experiences.name: Sahara Desert Camel Trek & Overnight Camp
experiences.description: Ride a camel into the golden Erg Chebbi dunes at sunset, arriving at a traditional Berber desert camp. Spend the night under an extraordinary canopy of stars, enjoy live Gnawa music around a campfire, and wake before dawn to climb the dunes for a breathtaking sunrise over the Sahara.

experiences.name: Bahia Palace & Saadian Tombs Historical Tour
experiences.description: Step back into Morocco's imperial past with a self-guided tour of the stunning 19th-century Bahia Palace, featuring intricate zellij tilework and carved cedarwood ceilings. Then visit the rediscovered Saadian Tombs, a lavishly decorated royal necropolis dating to the 16th century, hidden for centuries behind palace walls.

experiences.name: Traditional Moroccan Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a local chef for a hands-on cooking class in a riad kitchen. Start with a guided visit to the Mellah spice market to select fresh ingredients, then learn to prepare classic dishes like chicken tagine with preserved lemon, harira soup, and flaky bastilla. Enjoy your creations over mint tea.

experiences.name: Todra Gorge Rock Climbing & Hike
experiences.description: Venture to the dramatic Todra Gorge, where towering 300-meter rose-red canyon walls rise from a cool river valley. Hike through the narrow gorge passage, spot Barbary ground squirrels, and try beginner-friendly rock climbing routes on the canyon walls with a local guide. A thrilling natural adventure en route between Marrakech and the Sahara.
experiences.location: Todra Gorge, Tinghir Province, High Atlas

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 13:00. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the No. 19 public bus (approx 20 MAD) or shared grand taxi (approx 50-70 MAD split) to your accommodation. Check in, freshen up, and take a gentle orientation walk through your neighborhood to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Easy introduction to Marrakech: stroll to the legendary Djemaa el-Fna square at dusk to witness the transformation — snake charmers, storytellers, musicians, and food stalls lighting up. Absorb the atmosphere without spending much. Browse the edge of the souks without buying yet.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: Grab a quick snack at the airport or a street-side sandwich near the accommodation (msemen flatbread with cheese or olive tapenade, approx 10-15 MAD)
meals.dinner: Eat at the Djemaa el-Fna food stalls — hearty harira soup (5 MAD), grilled merguez sausages with bread (25 MAD), and fresh orange juice (4 MAD). Full meal under 50 MAD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Exchange some euros/dollars to Moroccan Dirhams (MAD) at the airport or a city bureau de change — avoid hotel exchange rates. Keep small bills handy for tips and street food. March weather in Marrakech is pleasant (18-24°C), so a light jacket for evenings is recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early and visit the stunning Koutoubia Mosque gardens (exterior only, free) at sunrise for golden light photography. Then head to the Ben Youssef Medersa, one of North Africa's largest Islamic schools — entry approx 70 MAD. Marvel at the intricate zellige tilework, stucco carvings, and cedar woodwork. Explore the nearby Almoravid Koubba (oldest standing monument in Marrakech, 20 MAD entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Lose yourself in the historic souks of the Medina. Navigate the dyers' souk (Souk Sabbaghin), the leather souk, the spice market, and the metalworkers' quarter. Practice your bargaining skills — start at 30-40% of the asking price. Visit the free Mouassine Fountain and the 16th-century Mouassine Mosque courtyard. Head to the Bahia Palace (70 MAD entry) for a fascinating glimpse into 19th-century Moroccan royal life.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from a rooftop café terrace overlooking the Medina (order a mint tea, approx 15-20 MAD, to earn your seat). Then wander back to Djemaa el-Fna for evening entertainment — the square is free to enjoy. Browse the second-hand book and map stalls.

meals.breakfast: At your accommodation or a local café — café au lait, msemen, and amlou (argan oil almond dip) for approx 25-35 MAD
meals.lunch: Local workers' restaurant in the Medina — a set lunch of tagine or couscous with bread and a drink for approx 40-60 MAD
meals.dinner: Djemaa el-Fna food stalls again or a small local restaurant (restaurant du peuple style) — lamb tagine with prunes for approx 55-70 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — Medina streets are uneven cobblestone. Be cautious of unofficial 'guides' who offer to show you around for free but then demand payment. The souks can be overwhelming; use the Koutoubia minaret as a navigation landmark.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the hauntingly beautiful ruins of the El Badi Palace (70 MAD entry), a 16th-century Saadian palace once described as one of the world's wonders. Climb the ramparts for panoramic Medina views. Nearby, visit the Saadian Tombs (70 MAD entry) — ornate royal mausoleums rediscovered in 1917, featuring spectacular carved plasterwork.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Mellah (Jewish quarter) to explore its distinctive architecture, the Lazama Synagogue (small donation appreciated), and the vibrant spice and gold jewelry market. Then take a petit taxi (approx 15-20 MAD) to the Majorelle Garden (150 MAD entry) — the iconic cobalt-blue villa and garden made famous by Yves Saint Laurent. The adjacent Berber Museum is included in the ticket.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Gueliz neighborhood (the French New Town) for a change of pace. Window shop on Avenue Mohammed V, then find a local café for a relaxing evening. Consider attending a free traditional Gnawa music performance if one is happening in the square.

meals.breakfast: Fresh-squeezed orange juice and beghrir (semolina pancakes with honey and butter) at a street stall near the Mellah — approx 20 MAD
meals.lunch: Sandwich shop near El Badi Palace — kefta (spiced meatball) sandwich with harissa for approx 20-30 MAD
meals.dinner: Budget restaurant in Gueliz — pasta or pizza at a local spot, or return to Medina for a traditional bissara (fava bean soup) with olive oil and cumin for approx 10 MAD, plus bread

day_by_day.notes: Majorelle Garden is the priciest single attraction on this trip but is genuinely iconic and worth the splurge. Book tickets online in advance to avoid queues. The garden is busiest 10am-12pm; late afternoon is more peaceful. Dress modestly when visiting religious sites.

day_by_day.date: Day 4 - 2027-03-18 (Travel to Sahara via Shared Transport)
day_by_day.morning: Early start — depart Marrakech by 07:00-08:00 via shared CTM bus or a budget shared minivan/grand taxi from Bab Ghmat bus station toward Ouarzazate (approx 80-100 MAD by CTM bus, 3.5 hours). Pass through the dramatic Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m elevation) with stunning Atlas Mountain scenery. Stop briefly at a roadside Berber village for photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Ouarzazate — the 'Hollywood of Africa.' Visit the free exterior of Aït Benhaddou (30-minute shared taxi from Ouarzazate, approx 20 MAD), the UNESCO World Heritage ksar (fortified village) used in Game of Thrones, Gladiator, and Lawrence of Arabia. Walk through the living ksar and climb to the top granary for panoramic views. Entry to the ksar itself is free; a local guide inside will ask for a small tip (20-30 MAD is generous).
day_by_day.evening: Continue by shared grand taxi or local bus from Ouarzazate toward Zagora or Merzouga (check routes — Merzouga for the classic Erg Chebbi dunes is approx 5-6 more hours, better done over two days; Zagora is 3 hours for a closer desert experience). Overnight in a budget guesthouse in Ouarzazate or en route (approx 100-150 MAD for a dorm bed or basic room).

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your Marrakech accommodation or a café near the bus station — coffee and a hard-boiled egg with bread for 15-20 MAD
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or roadside stop in the mountains — vendors sell nuts, dried fruit, and bread at pass viewpoints for 10-20 MAD
meals.dinner: Simple tagine at a local restaurant in Ouarzazate — chicken or vegetable tagine with bread for 50-70 MAD

day_by_day.notes: This is the longest travel day of the trip. Book your CTM bus ticket the day before from the Bab Doukkala terminal. Bring snacks, water, and a light layer for the mountain pass which can be chilly in March. The road over Tizi n'Tichka is spectacular but winding — sit by a window for best views and to avoid motion sickness.

day_by_day.date: Day 5 - 2027-03-19 (Journey to the Sahara & Desert Experience)
day_by_day.morning: Continue the journey toward the Sahara. If in Ouarzazate, take a shared grand taxi or local bus toward Zagora (approx 70-80 MAD, 3 hours) passing through the dramatic Draa Valley with its ancient kasbahs, palmeries, and oasis towns. Alternatively, head toward Merzouga via Erfoud if time allows. Stop at the Draa Valley palmeries for a short walk among the date palms.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at your desert base town (Zagora or M'hamid for Erg Chigaga; Merzouga for Erg Chebbi). Check into a budget auberge or desert camp (100-200 MAD for a basic room or Berber tent). Rent a local guide or join a small group for a camel trek into the dunes (budget operators offer 1-2 hour treks for 100-150 MAD per person). Ride into the sea of golden sand dunes as the afternoon light turns amber.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the Sahara sunset from the top of a dune — one of the most breathtaking free experiences on Earth. Return to the desert camp for a traditional Berber dinner around a campfire under an extraordinary star-filled sky (far from light pollution). Local musicians may play traditional Gnawa or Berber music. Sleep in a Berber tent under the stars.

meals.breakfast: At your guesthouse in Ouarzazate — mint tea, bread, olive oil, and jam for 20-30 MAD
meals.lunch: Roadside stop in the Draa Valley — fresh dates (buy direct from a local for 20-30 MAD per bag) and bread with cheese
meals.dinner: Included in most desert camp packages — communal Berber meal of tagine, couscous, and mint tea around the campfire. If not included, budget 70-100 MAD at the camp restaurant.

day_by_day.notes: Negotiate desert camp prices in advance — a basic Berber tent with dinner and breakfast often costs 200-300 MAD total per person from local operators (avoid tourist agencies in Marrakech which charge 5x more). Bring a warm layer — Sahara nights in March can drop to 5-10°C. Sandstorms are rare in March but pack a scarf/shemagh to protect your face during windy camel rides.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before dawn (around 06:00) to watch the Sahara sunrise from the dunes — the shifting colors from deep purple to fiery orange are unforgettable and completely free. Take a final short walk in the dunes, then return to camp for a Berber breakfast. Check out and begin the return journey toward Marrakech, stopping at interesting points along the way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at the fortified ksar of Tamnougalt in the Draa Valley (free to walk around exterior, small tip for the guardian if you enter, 20 MAD). Continue through the Valley of a Thousand Kasbahs. If returning via Ouarzazate, visit the Taourirt Kasbah (20 MAD entry) — a well-preserved 19th-century palace complex. Take a shared grand taxi or CTM bus back toward Marrakech (depart by 14:00-15:00 to arrive by evening).
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Marrakech tired but exhilarated. Treat yourself to a traditional hammam (public bath) experience at a local neighborhood hammam — Hammam Dar el-Bacha or a local quarter hammam costs just 15-25 MAD for the basic scrub and steam (bring your own kessa scrub glove and savon beldi black soap, available in the souks for 20 MAD total). Relax and recover.

meals.breakfast: At the desert camp — mint tea, msemen, honey, and argan oil (usually included in camp package)
meals.lunch: Packed snacks or a quick stop at a roadside café in the Draa Valley — harira soup and bread for 15-20 MAD
meals.dinner: Back in Marrakech — splurge slightly on a sit-down restaurant in the Medina. A proper Moroccan pastilla (sweet pigeon pie) or mechoui (slow-roasted lamb) at a mid-range local restaurant for 80-100 MAD as a treat after the desert adventure.

day_by_day.notes: The return journey from the Sahara to Marrakech is long (7-10 hours depending on your desert base). Consider breaking it up with stops rather than rushing. Grand taxis can be negotiated for the full route but confirm the price before departure. Keep your accommodation in Marrakech booked for this night.

day_by_day.morning: Visit any missed Marrakech highlights. Head to the Cyber Park (Arsat Moulay Abdeslam) — a free public garden with free WiFi, perfect for uploading photos and relaxing. Then explore the Mellah spice market one final time for last-minute souvenir shopping. Best budget souvenirs: saffron (genuine is sold in small quantities, 20-30 MAD), argan oil (buy from a women's cooperative for authenticity, 50-80 MAD for small bottle), leather keyring or wallet (bargain down to 30-50 MAD).
day_by_day.afternoon: Final souk shopping and packing. Visit the free Mouassine Museum of Living Arts if open (check current status). Take a final mint tea on a rooftop terrace and write postcards. Head to the post office (La Poste) near Djemaa el-Fna to mail them — stamps are cheap and it's a local experience. Begin making your way to the airport allowing plenty of time (take the No. 19 bus for 20 MAD or a petit taxi for 50-70 MAD).
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner before departure or at the airport. If time allows, one last stroll through Djemaa el-Fna at dusk. Depart from Marrakech Menara Airport. Reflect on an incredible week of culture, history, adventure, and desert magic.

meals.breakfast: Final traditional Moroccan breakfast at a local café — café au lait, fresh orange juice, msemen with honey and butter, and a hard-boiled egg for approx 30-40 MAD
meals.lunch: Quick lunch at a local restaurant near the souks — a bowl of harira, a briouate (fried pastry with cheese or meat), and mint tea for approx 35-45 MAD
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or a final street food feast at Djemaa el-Fna — mix of small plates: snail soup (5 MAD), fried fish (25 MAD), fresh orange juice (4 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at least 2.5 hours before departure. Keep some MAD for airport coffee/snacks as euros/dollars are not always accepted at small vendors. Any remaining MAD can be exchanged back at the airport (keep your exchange receipts). Total estimated budget for the 7-day trip excluding flights and accommodation: 1,500-2,500 MAD (approx €140-230 / $150-250 USD) covering transport, entry fees, food, and basic souvenirs.

trip_options.title: Classic Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara) Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Marrakech Menara Airport at 13:00 – no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort and check in. Freshen up and settle into your room.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a gentle orientation stroll through the nearby Gueliz (Ville Nouvelle) neighborhood. Explore Avenue Mohammed V, browse local boutiques, and get a feel for the city's rhythm. Visit a local pharmacy or souk stall to pick up essentials.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Djemaa el-Fna Square at dusk to witness the iconic transformation as street performers, storytellers, snake charmers, and food stalls come alive. Soak in the atmosphere and take photos of the vibrant chaos.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a light snack or coffee at the airport or hotel upon arrival
meals.lunch: Café de France on Djemaa el-Fna – classic Moroccan harira soup, fresh bread, and mint tea for around 80–120 MAD
meals.dinner: Eat at the open-air food stalls on Djemaa el-Fna Square – try grilled merguez sausages, kefta skewers, and fresh orange juice for an authentic and affordable experience (100–150 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Exchange currency at the airport or a nearby bureau de change. Keep small bills handy for the square vendors. March evenings can be cool, so bring a light jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the historic Medina of Marrakech. Visit the stunning Koutoubia Mosque (exterior), then walk through the ancient souks – Souk Semmarine, Souk des Teinturiers (Dyers' Quarter), and Souk Cherratin (leather workers). Hire a local guide for 150–200 MAD for a 2-hour tour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the magnificent Bahia Palace (45 MAD entry), a 19th-century masterpiece of Moroccan architecture with intricate tilework and painted ceilings. Afterward, explore the nearby Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and visit the Lazama Synagogue.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Saadian Tombs (70 MAD entry) before they close, then enjoy a traditional hammam experience at a mid-range local hammam such as Hammam Bab Doukkala – a full scrub and steam session for 150–250 MAD.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local café serving msemen (Moroccan flatbread), honey, argan oil, and café au lait
meals.lunch: Nomad Restaurant in the Medina – rooftop dining with modern Moroccan cuisine; tagine or couscous for 120–180 MAD
meals.dinner: Le Jardin restaurant in the Medina – dine in a beautiful riad garden setting with traditional Moroccan dishes for 200–300 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes – the Medina streets are cobblestoned and uneven. Bargaining is expected in the souks; start at 40–50% of the asking price.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Ourika Valley (45 min from Marrakech). Hire a private driver or join a shared tour (300–500 MAD). Walk along the Ourika River, visit a traditional Berber village, and explore a working argan oil cooperative where women demonstrate the traditional oil-making process.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue up the valley to the Setti Fatma waterfalls. Hike up to the first waterfall (30–45 min moderate trek) for panoramic views of the Atlas foothills. The scenery in March is lush and green.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Marrakech. Visit the Majorelle Garden and YSL Museum (150 MAD for the garden; 100 MAD for the museum). The electric-blue garden is magical in the late afternoon light. Browse the boutique gift shop for quality souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast – traditional Moroccan spread with msemen, beghrir (honeycomb pancakes), jam, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Riverside Berber restaurant in Ourika Valley – freshly grilled trout from the river, Berber bread, and salads for 100–150 MAD
meals.dinner: Café Clock Marrakech in the Medina – creative fusion Moroccan menu including their famous camel burger; budget 150–220 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Book the Ourika Valley transport the night before. Bring sunscreen and a hat for the waterfall hike. Majorelle Garden can get crowded – arrive just before it opens at 8am or after 4pm.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech early (7:00 AM) for the Sahara Desert via the Draa Valley and Dadès Gorge. Travel by private transfer or shared desert tour (1,200–2,000 MAD for a 3-day package). Stop at Aït Benhaddou, the UNESCO-listed ksar (fortified village) used in Game of Thrones and Gladiator. Explore the ancient mud-brick citadel for 1–2 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the dramatic Dadès Gorge and Roses Valley (famous for rose harvest in May, but still scenic in March). Stop at viewpoints overlooking the winding gorge roads known as 'the fingers of the monkey.' Pass through the Draa Valley date palm oases.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Merzouga (gateway to Erg Chebbi dunes) by early evening. Check into a mid-range desert camp or guesthouse. Mount camels for a 45-minute sunset ride into the Erg Chebbi dunes – the golden hour light on the dunes is extraordinary.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure – light continental spread
meals.lunch: Stop at a local restaurant in Ouarzazate – tagine with local vegetables and lamb for 80–120 MAD
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber dinner under the stars at your desert camp – harira soup, tagine, couscous, and Moroccan pastries with mint tea; typically included in camp packages

day_by_day.notes: This is a long travel day (approximately 8–9 hours of driving). Pack snacks and water. The Dadès Gorge road has dramatic hairpin bends – not recommended for those prone to motion sickness. Dress in layers as desert temperatures drop sharply after sunset.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before dawn (5:30 AM) to hike or ride to the top of a dune for a breathtaking Sahara sunrise. The silence and color gradients are unforgettable. Return to camp for a traditional Berber breakfast. Explore the Merzouga village and visit a local nomadic family if arranged through your camp.
day_by_day.afternoon: Adventure activities in the Erg Chebbi dunes: choose from sandboarding down the dunes, a 4x4 off-road dune excursion, or a guided quad bike ride (200–400 MAD per activity). Visit the Gnawa musicians' village near Merzouga for a cultural music session.
day_by_day.evening: Spend a second night at the desert camp. Participate in a traditional Gnawa drumming circle around the campfire. Stargaze in one of the darkest skies in Morocco – the Milky Way is clearly visible in March.

meals.breakfast: Berber camp breakfast – khobz bread, olive oil, honey, amlou (almond-argan paste), hard-boiled eggs, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a local Merzouga café – sandwiches, fresh juice, and tagine for 80–120 MAD
meals.dinner: Second desert camp dinner – traditional three-course Moroccan meal with live Berber music; included in most camp packages

day_by_day.notes: Bring a buff or scarf to protect against sand in the wind. Keep your camera and phone in a sealed bag when not in use. Sunscreen is essential as desert sun is intense even in March. The camp typically provides blankets but bring an extra layer for sleeping.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Merzouga after breakfast and travel north through the Ziz Valley and Todra Gorge. Stop at the spectacular Todra Gorge – towering 300-meter rock walls with a river running through. Take a 1-hour walk through the gorge floor; rock climbers can often be spotted on the walls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Dadès Valley (the 'Valley of a Thousand Kasbahs') back toward Marrakech via the High Atlas Mountains. Stop at the Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m elevation) for panoramic views. Arrive back in Marrakech by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a relaxing evening with a traditional hammam or spa treatment at the hotel or a nearby riad spa. Stroll through the Mellah or Gueliz for last-minute souvenir shopping.

meals.breakfast: Desert camp breakfast before early departure
meals.lunch: Traditional restaurant in Tinghir near Todra Gorge – Berber omelette, fresh salad, and tagine for 100–150 MAD
meals.dinner: Riad Yima in Marrakech Medina – run by artist Hassan Hajjaj, vibrant pop-art décor with traditional Moroccan small plates; 180–280 MAD

day_by_day.notes: The return drive from Merzouga to Marrakech is approximately 9 hours. Start early (7:00 AM) to avoid arriving too late. The Tizi n'Tichka pass can have fog or light rain in March – drive carefully or ensure your driver is experienced.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech. Visit the El Badi Palace ruins (70 MAD entry) – a 16th-century palace with impressive sunken gardens and stork nests. Then visit the Museum of Marrakech (Musée de Marrakech) housed in a beautiful 19th-century riad palace for 50 MAD.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last souk shopping session – pick up quality Moroccan crafts: hand-painted ceramics, leather goods from the tanneries, argan oil products, spices from Rahba Kedima spice square, and Berber rugs. Visit a reputable fixed-price shop if you want to avoid bargaining. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a rooftop restaurant with views over the Medina. Enjoy a final mint tea ceremony and pastilla (sweet pigeon pie) as a special send-off. Transfer to Marrakech Menara Airport for your departure flight.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast – full Moroccan spread as a final treat
meals.lunch: Terrasse des Épices – beautiful rooftop restaurant with panoramic Medina views; Moroccan salads, tagines, and bastilla for 150–250 MAD
meals.dinner: Dar Moha – elegant riad dining experience with live Gnawa music and a set menu of traditional Moroccan dishes for 350–500 MAD (splurge for the farewell night)

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5 hours before your flight for airport check-in and security. Keep 100–200 MAD in cash for airport tips and last-minute purchases. Declare any argan oil over 100ml in checked luggage. A wonderful trip – yallah!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara) Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Marrakech Menara Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort with a personal concierge welcome.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private check-in experience at the resort with a welcome mint tea ceremony. After settling in, enjoy a leisurely orientation stroll through the nearby Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and the ornate El Badi Palace exterior — a gentle introduction to Marrakech's layered history without overwhelming jet-lagged senses.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the resort's rooftop terrace overlooking the medina skyline. Private candlelit dinner at the resort's signature restaurant featuring refined Moroccan cuisine — bastilla au pigeon, slow-braised lamb tangia, and a curated selection of Moroccan wines and fresh-pressed juices.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight)
meals.lunch: Welcome light lunch at the resort upon arrival — mezze platters, harira soup, and fresh Moroccan pastries
meals.dinner: In-resort signature restaurant: multi-course Moroccan tasting menu with sommelier-paired beverages

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 relaxed to recover from travel. Confirm with concierge all upcoming private guide bookings and desert transfer logistics. Request a traditional hammam appointment for Day 2.

day_by_day.morning: Exclusive private guided tour of the Koutoubia Mosque gardens and the UNESCO-listed Bahia Palace. Your expert cultural historian guide provides in-depth context on Saadian and Alaouite dynasty architecture. Followed by a visit to the Saadian Tombs — arrive early to beat the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Immersive luxury hammam and spa treatment at a premium traditional bathhouse (e.g., Les Bains de Marrakech or the resort's own spa). Followed by a private guided exploration of the souks of the Medina — spice markets, leather tanneries, and artisan cooperatives — with a dedicated guide to navigate authentically and avoid tourist traps. Optional bespoke shopping with a personal stylist.
day_by_day.evening: Private rooftop dinner at a heritage riad restaurant such as La Maison Arabe or Dar Yacout — known for their atmospheric courtyard settings, live Gnawa music, and exquisite Moroccan gastronomy. Pre-dinner cocktails in the riad's lounge.

meals.breakfast: Lavish resort breakfast buffet: Moroccan msemen pancakes, amlou (argan almond dip), fresh-squeezed orange juice, eggs to order, and artisan pastries
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a premium medina café — Café des Épices or a private rooftop venue — fresh salads, briouats, and mint tea
meals.dinner: Heritage riad fine dining: pigeon pastilla, lamb mechoui, honey-glazed carrots, and almond-rose desserts

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the medina. The hammam session should be pre-booked. Carry small dirhams for tipping artisans. March weather in Marrakech is warm (~20–24°C) and pleasant.

day_by_day.morning: Private half-day excursion to the Majorelle Garden and the adjacent Yves Saint Laurent Museum (Musée Yves Saint Laurent Marrakech). Explore the cobalt-blue botanical paradise and the world-class fashion retrospective at your own pace with a private art and culture guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Musée de Marrakech housed in a stunning 19th-century palace, followed by a private cooking class in a traditional riad kitchen — learn to prepare harira, tagine, and traditional Moroccan sweets with a master chef. This is a hands-on cultural immersion experience.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private Fantasia (Tbourida) equestrian show — a UNESCO-recognized Moroccan tradition of horsemen in traditional dress performing synchronized cavalry charges. Followed by a lavish outdoor dinner under the stars at a premium venue such as Palais Namaskar or a private garden setting.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast: Berber omelette, honey and argan oil spread, freshly baked khobz bread, seasonal fruit platter
meals.lunch: Enjoy the dishes prepared during your own cooking class — a personalized and memorable culinary lunch
meals.dinner: Outdoor palace-style dinner: grilled kefta, slow-cooked lamb shoulder, Moroccan salad medley, pastilla au lait dessert, and rose water tea

day_by_day.notes: Book the Majorelle Garden tickets in advance — they sell out. The cooking class should be arranged through the concierge with a reputable local chef. Fantasia shows may vary by season; confirm availability.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech at 07:00 in a premium 4x4 luxury vehicle with a private driver-guide for the scenic journey to the Sahara Desert via the Draa Valley and Dades Gorges. Stop at the breathtaking Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m) in the High Atlas Mountains for panoramic photography and fresh mountain air.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the cinematic Draa Valley — a ribbon of date palms and kasbahs stretching through the desert. Stop at the UNESCO-listed Aït Benhaddou — the ancient fortified ksar (village) used as a filming location for Gladiator, Game of Thrones, and Lawrence of Arabia. Private guided tour with a local historian.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at the edge of the Sahara near Merzouga or Zagora (depending on route preference) and check into a luxury desert camp — a glamping experience with en-suite tented suites, private terraces, and plunge pools. Sunset camel trek into the Erg Chebbi dunes. Gourmet Berber dinner under a sky blazing with stars, accompanied by traditional Gnawa and Berber musicians around a bonfire.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure: continental spread with Moroccan pastries, yogurt, fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: Roadside authentic Berber lunch at a premium stop en route — tagine, Berber bread, and fresh-pressed juices at a curated local restaurant
meals.dinner: Luxury desert camp dinner: Berber slow-cooked lamb tagine, couscous with seven vegetables, Saharan salads, and traditional mint tea ceremony

day_by_day.notes: This is a long driving day (~7–8 hours with stops). Dress in layers — the Atlas Mountains can be cool in March. Bring sunscreen, sunglasses, and a scarf for the desert. Camel trek is approximately 45–60 minutes each way.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up for a private guided sunrise hike to the top of the Erg Chebbi sand dunes — one of the most spectacular natural spectacles in North Africa. Watch the Sahara ignite in shades of amber, gold, and crimson. Return to camp for a lavish breakfast in the dunes. Optional: sunrise hot-air balloon ride over the Sahara (premium add-on, must be pre-booked).
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided 4x4 desert adventure through the Sahara — visit nomadic Berber families, explore fossil-rich rocky desert terrain, and discover hidden desert oases. Visit the Merzouga village and a local artisan cooperative specializing in silver jewelry and desert crafts. Afternoon rest and spa treatment at the luxury camp.
day_by_day.evening: Private astronomy session with a local expert astronomer — the Sahara offers some of the clearest night skies on Earth. Spot constellations, planets, and the Milky Way with telescope access. Followed by a candlelit private dinner in the dunes — a truly once-in-a-lifetime romantic and adventurous experience.

meals.breakfast: Desert camp breakfast: fresh-baked Berber bread, honey, dates, goat cheese, eggs, and Saharan herbal tea served in the dunes
meals.lunch: Camp lunch: light mezze, grilled meats, Moroccan salads, and fresh fruit under a shaded Bedouin tent
meals.dinner: Private candlelit dune dinner: premium Moroccan cuisine with curated Moroccan wines or premium non-alcoholic infusions

day_by_day.notes: Temperatures in the Sahara in March can drop significantly at night (5–10°C) — pack a warm layer. The hot-air balloon must be booked weeks in advance. Respect nomadic family privacy when visiting — your guide will advise on etiquette.

day_by_day.morning: Depart the desert camp after breakfast and begin the scenic return journey toward Marrakech via the Todra Gorge — towering 300-meter rock walls carved by the Todra River. Private guided walk through the narrow gorge with a geologist-guide explaining the dramatic landscape formation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at the Roses Valley (Vallée des Roses) near Kelaat M'Gouna — in mid-March the damask rose fields are beginning to bloom, and the air is fragrant with rose essence. Visit a traditional rose water distillery and purchase artisan rose products. Continue through the Skoura Oasis — a vast palm grove dotted with ancient kasbahs — for a late afternoon exploration.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Marrakech and check back into the Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a restorative luxury spa session — traditional argan oil massage and rose hammam treatment. Elegant dinner at a premium Marrakech restaurant — Le Tobsil or Nomad's rooftop — celebrating the desert adventure.

meals.breakfast: Final desert camp breakfast: dates, Berber pancakes, argan oil, fresh juices, and coffee
meals.lunch: Scenic roadside lunch in the Todra Gorge area at a curated restaurant — fresh trout from the Todra River (a local specialty), salads, and bread
meals.dinner: Premium Marrakech restaurant: refined contemporary Moroccan cuisine — slow-roasted lamb, preserved lemon chicken, and a decadent pastilla au lait for dessert

day_by_day.notes: The return drive is approximately 6–7 hours with stops. Roses Valley timing is perfect in March — a unique seasonal highlight. Confirm spa appointment with resort concierge during the drive back.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech — leisurely resort breakfast followed by a private guided visit to the Menara Gardens and Agdal Gardens, royal olive groves and reflecting pools dating to the 12th century. A peaceful, photogenic farewell to the city. Optional: final souvenir shopping in the Gueliz (New City) district for premium Moroccan crafts, leather goods, and argan products.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a farewell luxury lunch. Final packing, check-out, and private luxury transfer to Marrakech Menara Airport. Time permitting, enjoy a final mint tea in the resort's courtyard and reflect on an extraordinary week.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Marrakech Menara Airport. Evening flight home with memories of imperial cities, golden dunes, and the timeless magic of Morocco.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell resort breakfast: full Moroccan and international spread — pastries, eggs, smoked salmon, fresh juices, and specialty coffees
meals.lunch: Premium farewell lunch at the resort or a top Marrakech restaurant: a curated selection of Moroccan favorites — tagine, couscous, and a final pastilla
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight meal (departure dependent)

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for airport check-in and security. Request the concierge to arrange a premium airport lounge pass if available. Ensure all purchased artisan goods are properly wrapped for travel. Carry argan oil and rose water in checked luggage to comply with liquid restrictions.
